doc.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Trumpet battles: Carter, Newman, Anderson and the Trumpet Kings
summary: Williams cites Benny Carter's pairing in Japan; Peterson describes the Trumpet Kings studio date and Montreux night with Basie's warning.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Exciting. I saw Benny Carter do the same thing with Joe Newman, and Cat Anderson. You wouldn’t think that that duo would do it, but it’s one of the most exciting things you ever want to hear. The Japanese went crazy.
You know, went absolutely crazy. Seventeen thousand of them, you know?

We did, the trumpet kings, in the studio, and then he did it again in Montreux. He had Clark Terry, Dizzy, right, and Roy, and Basie’s remarks that night, he was on the bill that night and Basie’s remark that night before we came out was, “okay now the trumpets are up next,” and Basie was sitting in a chair, you know how he’d sort of sit and overlook the whole situation, but he says [smacks his lips] “somebody’s gonna get hurt tonight.” He said, “somebody’s gonna get it.”
But it made music, and some of the most exciting things that ever were played, and everybody was excited about it.
That’s right. Because you stretched, you know. No matter what happens, you’re playing your thing, that’s one thing. You’re doing what you know you do and you’re in that
particular sphere. But when somebody else enters your sphere of operation, then it becomes—
